items.headline: Houthi strikes hit Saudi airports and oil sites
items.summary: Houthi rebels struck Saudi airports, killing three people and wounding dozens, as Yemen's war escalates. Earlier strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure are adding to regional tension and pushing oil prices up.

items.headline: Russian strike on a Ukrainian bus kills 30
items.summary: Russian attacks in eastern Ukraine, including a strike on a public bus, killed 30 people, while power outages in Kyiv are getting worse.

items.headline: South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine and tests a hypersonic weapon
items.summary: Seoul is pulling its ambassador from Kyiv over a dispute about North Korean prisoners of war. Separately, South Korea flight-tested its first homegrown hypersonic weapon after a North Korean hypersonic launch and mine blasts that wounded three South Korean soldiers.

items.headline: Isaias becomes a hurricane as the Gulf Coast prepares
items.summary: Isaias has strengthened into a hurricane, and Gulf Coast residents are preparing for storms. Forecasters had said a week ago that the Atlantic might go the whole season without a hurricane.

items.headline: Midterms: about 60 House seats will decide control, and Kansas is now a Senate battleground
items.summary: Both parties are concentrating money on roughly 60 House districts that Trump carried by about nine points on average in 2024. In Kansas, Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces a tightening race against Democrat Adam Hamilton.

items.headline: Trump's $90 Medicare rebate rolls out, but millions don't qualify
items.summary: The administration is sending one-time $90 payments toward Medicare Part B premiums at an estimated cost of $2 billion. Many enrollees aren't eligible, and critics call it a political stunt ahead of the midterms.

items.headline: ICE quietly used a New Jersey warehouse as a detention site, neighbors say
items.summary: An NPR investigation examines local accounts that ICE ran a detention facility out of a warehouse in Roxbury, New Jersey, over the summer. The report raises questions about oversight of temporary detention sites.

items.headline: A $110 billion Skydance deal for Warner Bros. Discovery
items.summary: The Ellison family's proposed purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, owner of CNN and the Warner studio, would concentrate control over major news and entertainment outlets. Critics argue it would leave less room for dissent.

items.headline: Syrian general accused of atrocities shielded in Lebanon, NPR and BBC find
items.summary: A joint NPR and BBC investigation found that a former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity lives in Lebanon. The report says he has been financed and protected by U.S. and Lebanese authorities.

items.headline: French students invoke May 1968 in school-funding protests
items.summary: Students protesting underfunded schools in France are carrying signs that reference the 1968 uprising that nearly brought down the government. More than 250,000 people have marched over education reforms, class sizes and building conditions.

digest.overview:
At home, Isaias has strengthened into a hurricane and Gulf Coast residents are preparing for the storm ahead of a weekend Georgia-Alabama game Trump plans to attend. In politics, both parties are pouring money into about 60 competitive House districts, Kansas has become an unexpected Senate battleground, and Georgia's governor candidates Keisha Lance Bottoms and Rick Jackson met in their only televised debate. The administration's one-time $90 Medicare rebate is rolling out, though millions of enrollees don't qualify. An NPR investigation reports ICE quietly ran a detention site out of a New Jersey warehouse this summer. In business, the Ellison family's $110 billion Skydance deal for Warner Bros. Discovery is drawing media-concentration concerns, and the regulator for crypto and prediction markets is shrinking as those markets grow. Actor Eva Marie Saint, star of 'On the Waterfront,' died at 102.

Abroad, Houthi rebels struck Saudi airports, killing three and injuring 36, after earlier attacks on Saudi oil sites that pushed oil prices up. In Ukraine, Russian strikes including one on a public bus killed 30 people as blackouts worsen in Kyiv. South Korea said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine in a dispute over North Korean prisoners of war, and it test-flew its first homegrown hypersonic weapon after a North Korean hypersonic test and border mine blasts that injured three South Korean soldiers. An NPR and BBC investigation found a Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity living under protection in Lebanon. In France, student protests over school funding are drawing comparisons to May 1968, and Indonesia is restricting access to forest data as deforestation surges.

home.overview:
Baseball's final four is nearly set. The Dodgers closed out the Braves and will meet the Brewers in the NLCS, which eliminated the Padres, while the Rays swept the Yankees and await the winner of tonight's Game 4 between the White Sox (up 2–1) and Guardians. In the NFL, Thursday night features the winless Buccaneers at Dallas, with rookie QB Jalon Daniels starting for Tampa. The Chiefs, 49ers and Vikings are still unbeaten at 4–0, while Lamar Jackson and Ja'Marr Chase are uncertain for Sunday. The NBA season tips off Oct. 20, with Giannis Antetokounmpo starting his first year in Miami.

Club soccer returns this weekend after the international break, headlined by Liverpool vs. Man City on Sunday, with City perfect at 5–0 despite being found guilty on 114 Premier League charges, which the club is appealing. Barcelona are 7–0 in La Liga, and Dortmund lead the Bundesliga. In the break, England beat Croatia 7–0, the USA edged Canada 1–0 and South Korea beat Uzbekistan 2–0. In K League 1, FC Seoul lead by 15 points and host third-place Jeju on Saturday. The Champions League resumes Oct. 13–14.

brief: NLCS set: the Dodgers face the Brewers starting around Oct 11. LA beat Atlanta 4–1 in Game 4 to close out the series.
Milwaukee eliminated San Diego with a 3–1 win in Game 4 at Petco Park.
The Rays swept the Yankees, taking Game 3 4–3 in the Bronx. Aaron Boone's team is out.
White Sox vs. Guardians Game 4 is tonight in Chicago. Cleveland stayed alive with a 9–3 win, and the winner meets Tampa Bay in the ALCS.
Freddie Freeman and Enrique Hernández homered and Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched well as the Dodgers won Game 3.

Still unbeaten: Chiefs, 49ers and Vikings (4–0). Still winless: Bucs, Chargers, Dolphins, Texans and Titans.
Injury watch: Lamar Jackson and Ja'Marr Chase are uncertain for Sunday. Jayden Daniels practiced fully and may return for Washington.

The Eagles are dismantling their offensive line and stockpiling picks, and many now see it as a full rebuild.
Last week: the Falcons routed the Saints 45–24 on Monday night, and the Panthers upset the Lions 32–26 on Sunday night.

brief: Club football returns this weekend after the international break. The headline match is Liverpool vs. Man City on Sunday.
Man City lead the Premier League with five wins from five, even after a commission found the club guilty on 114 charges. City are appealing.
Barcelona have won all seven La Liga games. Real Madrid sit 4th after losing the derby 2–1 to Atlético. Dortmund lead the Bundesliga at 4–0.
European nights resume next week: Champions League on Oct 13–14, then Europa League Matchday 2 and the Conference League opener on Oct 15.
National teams: England beat Croatia 7–0 and Czechia 3–0 in the Nations League. The USA beat Canada 1–0 on Justin Ellis's winner, and South Korea beat Uzbekistan 2–0.
MLS: Nashville lead the league with 60 points, 10 clear of Vancouver, as the regular season winds down.
K League 1: FC Seoul lead by 15 points and host 3rd-place Jeju on Saturday. In K League 2, Suwon Samsung top the promotion race.
